name: Ishmael
overview: Ishmael is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Zebadiah, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 19:11. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not specified here, his role as a father is a notable aspect of his identity.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishmael means "G-d [El] he heard," reflecting a recognition of God's attention. This is the only recorded name for him, indicating its significance as a proper name without additional titles.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ishmael as the father of Zebadiah, according to 2 Chronicles 19:11. Beyond this, no other family relationships are detailed in the given information.
scriptureSignificance: Ishmael holds an important place in biblical history as the son of Abraham through Hagar, Sarah's maidservant. Though not the child of promise, God made a covenant to bless him and his descendants, making him the father of twelve princes. His life and legacy highlight the contrast between human effort and God's sovereign plan, especially in relation to his half-brother Isaac, illustrating the spiritual tension between the flesh and the Spirit.

keyEvents.event: God's promise to make him a great nation
